items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: the A&R man, who was Herman Diaz, was on the verge of losing his job, and so he was trying to do something to save his job

ctx.x: I also recorded "Earth Angel" with a group called the Penguins, which was a big hit. I did "Summer Winds" with Wayne Newton; I recorded a song that -- now here's a story for you -- I did the "Colonel Bogie's March" with Mitch Miller, which was a big hit. They wanted a field drum sound -- I was always figuring out sounds and things, and so they wanted a field drum sound, but they didn't have a field drum there, and I don't know where I got the idea from, but it dawned on me, and I said to Jimmy Carroll, who was an…

Then I did another record that sold almost two million records -- that was Perez Prado, a tune called "Patricia". That was another thing where they had these tapes that were recorded out in California, and the A&R man, who was Herman Diaz, was on the verge of losing his job, and so

he was trying to do something to save his job, and he got this guitar player, Billy Muir, to -- in fact, that was one of the first times that I knew of that they did a thing called overdubbing, and it was the first time I ever heard a base guitar on a recording. It was Billy Muir, Alan Hannon and myself.
